summary: Turns the search page into a client component. It reads q from the URL, fetches matching products and renders them in a list.

findings.title: Search query injected as raw HTML
findings.description: The heading puts the q URL parameter into the page as unescaped HTML. Nothing sanitizes the query first. An attacker can send a crafted search link that runs script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS. Render the query as a text child so React escapes it.

findings.fix: Render the query as a text child so React escapes it.

findings.title: Effect refetches on every render
findings.description: The effect has no dependency list, so it runs after every render. Each run sets a new results array, which triggers another render. Every visit to the search page sends requests to the products API in an endless loop. This wastes client and server resources. Pass [query] as the effect's dependency list.

findings.title: Hooks called after a conditional return
findings.description: The component returns early when q is empty, before useState and useEffect run. The number of hook calls therefore changes between renders. React throws a hooks-order error when q goes from empty to set during client navigation. The page then crashes. Call useState and useEffect before the early return. Inside the effect, skip the fetch when query is empty.

findings.title: Search form removed with no replacement
findings.description: The change deletes the only search input form in the repository. The empty-query branch asks users to type a term but shows no input. Users who open the search page have no way to enter a query. Search is reachable only by editing the URL. Keep the form with input name q on this page, or add one elsewhere.

findings.title: Search promise rejection unhandled
findings.description: The searchProducts function throws when the response is not ok. The effect chains no catch, so the rejection is never handled. A failed search leaves stale or empty results with no error shown to the user. The browser only logs an unhandled rejection. Add a catch handler that records an error state and render a message for it.

findings.fix: Add a catch handler that records an error state and render a message for it.

findings.title: Search params read without a Suspense boundary
findings.description: The page calls useSearchParams with no Suspense boundary around it. Next 15 requires one for prerendered pages. The production build can fail on the search route with a missing Suspense boundary error. Move the client logic into a child component. Render that component inside Suspense from the page.

findings.title: New search behaviour has no covering test
findings.description: SearchPage now fetches and renders results and handles an empty query. The change adds no test for this behaviour. Regressions in query handling and result rendering will go unnoticed. Add a component test covering the empty query, a successful search and a failed search.
